item.title: NSW Waratahs claim historic seventh title with strong performance over Fijian Drua
item.description: The NSW Waratahs have come home strongly in the Super Rugby Women’s final, a disciplined and focused performance seeing them prevail 34-17 over the Fijian Drua in Ba. The Fijian fans showed again why they are some of the most passionate in world rugby, with a 4,097-strong crowd welcoming both sides to Ba.
item.content:encoded:
The NSW Waratahs have come home strongly in the Super Rugby Women’s final, a disciplined and focused performance seeing them prevail 34-17 over the Fijian Drua in Ba.

The Fijian fans showed again why they are some of the most passionate in world rugby, with a 4,097-strong crowd welcoming both sides to Ba.

However, despite coming into the weekend having done finals the hard way, the Waratahs started well, with Maya Stewart getting the visitors on the board inside the first 20 minutes.

Both sides saw plenty of opportunities to score, but the Drua’s handling errors and issues at the lineout proved a critical point of difference, and in the 28th minute the visitors went further ahead thanks to a strong effort from Desiree Miller.

The Drua pushed hard in the final ten minutes, however some brilliant cover defence by Caitlyn Halse saw the visitors hold on to take a 12-0 lead into the break.

The Drua’s errors continued early in the second half, with a knock on early in the second half on their own try line seeing Faliki Pohiva, who had put on several big hits in a player-of-the-match performance, scoring the Waratahs’ third in the 47th minute.

The backs then continued their form, with Rosie Ferguson cutting the defensive line to pieces five minutes later to score the Waratahs’ fourth – the score jumping out to a 24-0 lead.

The hosts turned to their forwards to make the hard yards, and found some success when Nunia Daunimoala barged over on the hour mark to give the hosts a sniff with 20 minutes to play.

However, a stunning double to substitute Amelia Whittaker in five minutes put the visitors out to a 34-5 lead with ten minutes to play.

Daunimoala would score a second try for the hosts with ten minutes to play, but the Waratahs wound the clock down well, Sulita Waisega managing only one more try after the siren to give the crowd something to cheer about.

Holding back tears, Bitila Tawake earned plenty of love from the home crowd on a special day for the competition.

“It took us five years to get the home grand final, and I’m sorry we didn’t get the win today,” Tawake said.

“The Waratahs, the best of the best. We gave our one hundred, you gave your one hundred, but at the end of the day, you guys won.

“The goal for the club is to get another grand final, and I promise we’ll get that again.”

“We dream at home of playing in front of crowds like you guys,” NSW Waratahs captain Chancellor said in accepting the title.

“You know how to support rugby, to come out and be so loud and so energetic, it lights my heart to know how much support women’s rugby has.

“Everytime we come out and play Fiji, we know we’re gonna have an incredible game. The way you play, with direct rugby, creative offloads, it’s a really tough game to play.

“We had 15 coaches and 40+ players that have contributed to this [season], we have 34 girls that have taken the field this season, and we’ve had six girls that have had injuries that have put them out or made it a really tough season for them.

“I want to shoutout every single player that’s been part of this program this year.

“Rugby in Australia wrote us off, we lose two games and that’s it for us. This is that response and I’m so proud of this team!”

item.title: Legge confident Drua ready for final challenge
item.description: MCDONALD’S Fijian Drua Women head coach Mike Legge believes his side is well prepared for today’s Super W final against the NSW Waratahs, with the team eager to make the most of home advantage at 4R Stadium in Ba. Speaking after the captain’s run yesterday, Legge said the squad completed its final preparations on a positive note after a focused week leading into the championship decider.
item.content:encoded:
MCDONALD’S Fijian Drua Women head coach Mike Legge believes his side is well prepared for today’s Super W final against the NSW Waratahs, with the team eager to make the most of home advantage at 4R Stadium in Ba.

Speaking after the captain’s run yesterday, Legge said the squad completed its final preparations on a positive note after a focused week leading into the championship decider.

“We finished our preparation with the captain’s run and it went really well,” Legge said.

“It has been a week where we tried to minimise distractions, and we’re looking forward to getting out there tomorrow.”

Drua captain Kolora Lomani admitted there are plenty of emotions within the camp, but said the team is excited for the occasion.

“Excited. The nerves are starting to kick in and we are looking forward to the game,” Lomani said.

She added that while some nervousness was expected, the players are now fully focused on the task ahead.

“Everyone was a bit nervous at the start of the week, but the girls are now looking forward to it.”

Lomani also called on supporters to pack 4R Stadium and help lift the Drua in what promises to be a historic occasion for women’s rugby in Fiji.

“Hope to see you at 4R Stadium. Hopefully we give you a good game.”

The Drua will be aiming to create history by winning their first Super W title on home soil, with a capacity crowd expected to roar the Fijian side on in Ba.

item.title: Binnu’s title defence headlines program
item.description: DEFENDING WBA Oceania super bantamweight champion Junior Binnu Singh will headline tonight’s King Boxing Promotion Bad Blood after the cancellation of Mikaele Ravalaca’s scheduled title fight. Binnu will defend his regional crown against Harjot Singh. The bout is now the feature fight of the promotion.
item.content:encoded:
DEFENDING WBA Oceania super bantamweight champion Junior Binnu Singh will headline tonight’s King Boxing Promotion Bad Blood after the cancellation of Mikaele Ravalaca’s scheduled title fight.

Binnu will defend his regional crown against Harjot Singh. The bout is now the feature fight of the promotion.

The late change follows the withdrawal of Ravalaca’s overseas opponents.

Promoter Naroon Buksh said replacement challenger Mahesh Dingari of India failed to board his flight. Another last-minute replacement from New Zealand also did not arrive.

“We have a dramatic change in the program. Our main bout is not taking place,” Buksh said.

“I arranged replacements from India and New Zealand, but neither turned up. I had no local opponent for Mika.”

Instead, Ravalaca will take part in an exhibition contest. Four local boxers will each face him over two rounds in a format approved by the World Boxing Association and the Boxing Commission of Fiji.

Buksh confirmed Binnu’s title defence would now close the show.

“The main bout has changed now. Binnu Singh will be fighting the main bout,” he said.

Other changes have also been made to the fight card because of weight issues and non-appearances. The Boxing Commission of Fiji is expected to confirm the final programme before tomorrow’s event.

Despite the setbacks, Buksh is confident fans will still enjoy the promotion.

“There are some changes, but the boxing spirit is always there. If you want to watch boxing tomorrow, please come down and support,” he said.

With the spotlight now on him, Binnu has the opportunity to defend his WBA Oceania super bantamweight title and cap off an event that has overcome significant last-minute challenges.

Gates open at 2pm with the action beginning at 4pm at the Vodafone Arena in Suva.

item.title: Moment to cherish
item.description: IT was a moment that David “Tolu” Young and Anahira McCutcheon will cherish forever. The two swimming stars proudly led Team Fiji into the Opening Ceremony of the 23rd Commonwealth Games at the OVO Hydro Arena in Glasgow, Scotland, yesterday, carrying the nation’s hopes onto one of the biggest stages in international sport.
item.content:encoded:
IT was a moment that David “Tolu” Young and Anahira McCutcheon will cherish forever.

The two swimming stars proudly led Team Fiji into the Opening Ceremony of the 23rd Commonwealth Games at the OVO Hydro Arena in Glasgow, Scotland, yesterday, carrying the nation’s hopes onto one of the biggest stages in international sport.

Young had the honour of carrying the Fiji flag, while McCutcheon bore the Commonwealth King’s Baton as Team Fiji marched alongside athletes from 74 nations and territories to officially launch the Games.

The historic ceremony, held indoors for the first time in Commonwealth Games history due to a compressed competition schedule, was brought to life by performances from Scottish artists KT Tunstall and Nina Nesbitt, before King Charles III and Queen Camilla made a dramatic entrance in a Doctor Who-inspired TARDIS.

Officially opening the Games, King Charles III described the Commonwealth as “a unique and extraordinary family of nations” and praised the athletes’ dedication, saying their perseverance would inspire people across the Commonwealth.

For Young and McCutcheon, leading Team Fiji into the arena was fitting recognition for years of hard work and outstanding performances in the pool.

Young has emerged as one of Fiji’s leading swimmers after winning three silver medals at the 2023 Pacific Games and setting a national record at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games.

At the 2025 Pacific Mini Games, he amassed two gold and four silver medals before going on to claim three golds at this year’s Oceania Swimming Championships.

McCutcheon has enjoyed an equally impressive rise.

The young swimmer won four silver and five bronze medals at the 2023 Pacific Games before representing Fiji at the Paris Olympics.

As the Fiji flag flew high inside the OVO Hydro, Young and McCutcheon stood proudly at the front of the national delegation, signalling the start of Team Fiji’s campaign at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games and the nation’s quest for success over the next 11 days.

item.title: International Secondary overcomes Tailevu North
item.description: INTERNATIONAL Secondary School held its nerve to defeat Tailevu North 4-1 in a penalty shootout after the teams finished locked 1-1 in the under-19 Southern Zones Secondary Schools football playoffs at the Ratu Cakobau park yesterday. The match remained evenly contested throughout the match, with both sides creating chances before the contest was decided from the penalty spot.
item.content:encoded:
INTERNATIONAL Secondary School held its nerve to defeat Tailevu North 4-1 in a penalty shootout after the teams finished locked 1-1 in the under-19 Southern Zones Secondary Schools football playoffs at the Ratu Cakobau park yesterday.

The match remained evenly contested throughout the match, with both sides creating chances before the contest was decided from the penalty spot.

International’s goalkeeper emerged as the hero, producing a crucial save to deny Tailevu North from the spot and leave its opponents with just one successful penalty. International converted four of its spot kicks to seal the victory.

Team manager for International Secondary School Simon Topham praised his players for their determination, especially considering their limited preparation heading into the competition.

“They haven’t really played matches on a full-sized 11-a-side pitch before. It’s one of the first matches they’ve played together as a team, so to come away with a victory is excellent.”

Topham admitted the team’s build-up to the competition had been disrupted by the recent four-week school break.

“It wasn’t ideal because we’ve just had a four-week school break and we’ve only been back at school for one week,” he said.

“They’ve done a lot of training over the last week, but they’ve done really well to come together.

Despite the victory, he said there was still room for improvement.

“They need to build their strength, conditioning and resilience, and continue working together as a team.”

International will now shift its focus to next week’s clash against Vashist Muni College.

item.title: Ravalaca to face four boxers after title fight collapse
item.description: WBA Oceania lightweight champion Mikaele Ravalaca will no longer defend his regional title after his Indian opponent, Mahesh Digari, withdrew from tomorrow night’s King Boxing Promotion Bad Blood event at Vodafone Arena in Suva. Digari was drafted in as a replacement after fellow Indian Rohit Chauhan pulled out of the main event.
item.content:encoded:
WBA Oceania lightweight champion Mikaele Ravalaca will no longer defend his regional title after his Indian opponent, Mahesh Digari, withdrew from tomorrow night’s King Boxing Promotion Bad Blood event at Vodafone Arena in Suva.

Digari was drafted in as a replacement after fellow Indian Rohit Chauhan pulled out of the main event.

However, Digari failed to travel to Fiji, leaving organisers without an opponent for Ravalaca.

Promoter Naroon Buksh said every effort had been made to save the title fight.

“Rohit pulled out and I signed Mahesh Dhingari. He did not board the plane,” Buksh said.

“I also arranged another boxer from New Zealand, but he did not appear. I had no alternative local opponent for Mika.”

Buksh also revealed that they had approached Runqi Zhou who had defeated Binu Singh and the late Ubayd Haider.

Negotiations collapsed when he knew he will be fighting Ravalaca.

“We had approached Zhou’s camp, and he was training in Chine,” Buksh said.

“He’s on 61 kg so when they heard his fighting Mika suddenly his weight went down. He said I’m at 57 and my price will be like $20,000 USD.”

Instead, Ravalaca will feature in a special exhibition contest against four local boxers, with each opponent contesting two rounds.

The four are Jone Tabuarua, Peni Vunisa, Watisoni Rokotuitoga and Samuela Leqaiwai.

Despite the disappointment, Ravalaca remains eager to step into the ring.

“It’s disappointing the opponent pulled out,” he said.

“Of course I’ll fight. I’ll show my skills and focus on myself.”

While Ravalaca’s title defence is off, the Fijian champion will still have the opportunity to showcase his talent before the home crowd.

item.title: Cakaudrove U20 through to semi-finals
item.description: THE Cakaudrove U20 team secured a hard-fought 24-13 victory over Tavua in their Vanua Challenge U20 quarter-finals match at Buckhurst Park Two in Suva on Wednesday, booking their third consecutive semi-final appearance. Despite the victory, team captain and openside flanker Taniela Tora emphasized the need for immediate improvements as they prepare for the semi-finals.
item.content:encoded:
THE Cakaudrove U20 team secured a hard-fought 24-13 victory over Tavua in their Vanua Challenge U20 quarter-finals match at Buckhurst Park Two in Suva on Wednesday, booking their third consecutive semi-final appearance.

Despite the victory, team captain and openside flanker Taniela Tora emphasized the need for immediate improvements as they prepare for the semi-finals.

“The number of penalties we conceded today (Wednesday) was disappointing,” Tora said.

“When we regroup, we will discuss our performance and what we need to improve before the semi-finals.”

Cakaudrove’s disciplined and composed effort kept them in control for most of the game, though Tavua showed strong determination in the second half.

The northerners’ steadfast defence ultimately denied the westerners any chance of a comeback.

Tora also expressed gratitude for the team’s strength and unity on the field. “I take this time to thank the Lord Almighty for the victory, for giving us the strength, the heart, and the ability to play as a team today,” he said.

Looking ahead, the team remains focused on their goal of winning the Vanua Challenge U20 competition this season after reaching three consecutive semi-finals in prior years.

item.title: Yat Sen edge Suva Grammar boys
item.description: DEFENDING champions Yat Sen Secondary School ended their campaign in the Suva zone 2 netball competition with a hard-fought 14-12 victory over Suva Grammar School at the netball centre in Suva. Team captain Jeremy Mar believes there is still room for improvement after a tight encounter yesterday. The narrow win gave Yat Sen a boost as they look to retain the central rally title they won last year.
item.content:encoded:
DEFENDING champions Yat Sen Secondary School ended their campaign in the Suva zone 2 netball competition with a hard-fought 14-12 victory over Suva Grammar School at the netball centre in Suva. Team captain Jeremy Mar believes there is still room for improvement after a tight encounter yesterday.

The narrow win gave Yat Sen a boost as they look to retain the central rally title they won last year.

Mar said the team had prepared well despite facing a few challenges leading into the tournament.

“I think it’s been really well. There were a few hiccups here and there, but it showed because we won today,” he said.

Despite the victory, Mar rated the team’s performance seven out of 10, saying improvements were needed ahead of the central school’s rally.

“Maybe our footwork and our obstructions need to improve. Other than that, I think we’re really good with everything.”

The team captain who is playing the position of goalkeeper said the team’s focus was to continue building on its performance and take each match as it comes.

“Our goal is to do what we did today, come out first, finish victorious and play one game at a time.”

Having lifted the championship trophy last year, Yat Sen enters this year’s competition with high expectations.

Mar said the team was determined to defend its crown but remained focused on the immediate task ahead.

“We won the rallies last year, so we’re hoping to win again this year,” he said.

Yat Sen will now turn its attention to the central rallies next week.
